title: A gate that names a host setup in its question is checked on that host or says why not
goal: backlog.py gate add refuses or start warns for a gate whose question or option text names a host setup (a runner, a signed-in CLI, a Windows host, an installed tool) and that carries no --host-check command and no recorded reason it cannot be checked, so the host-check of ST-26w7hg5u covers gates filed as free text too; a planted gate in test_backlog.py shows the refusal or warning and a gate with --host-check or a reason passes
notes: Left from ST-26w7hg5u "A gate that names a host setup is checked on that host before the sprint starts": gate add --host-check CMD and backlog.py host-check SP cover only gates that carry the command, and a gate whose host setup is named only in free text is not flagged. Premise, run before a sprint commits this story: python3 _tools/backlog.py gate add on an item with a question naming a host setup and no --host-check exits 0 and python3 _tools/backlog.py start accepts the sprint (run in a temp backlog). Open design: which words count as naming a host setup, and whether the answer is a refusal or a warning. Needs the operator's call on that heuristic, so record it as a gate when the story is planned into a sprint. The backlog.py split sprint SP-tpulmoxh moves the code: rebase this story's touches onto the new modules before claiming it. OPERATOR ANSWER 2026-10-04: WARN first (start and check warn, no refusal until two weeks of evidence); words that count as a host setup: host, service, daemon, credential, login, installed, enabled; the story is the start-warning form (bl_plan), not a refusal in gate add.
